proof:
# Small third fibers between two equal-volume simplices: all halfspaces

Historical claim of scope (pending review here): a scoped theorem, not the unrestricted OC theorem. For every
integer d>=2 there is a positive number rho_d such that the exact OC
constant holds for the three fibers described below whenever their small
endpoint has relative volume at most rho_d. The point is explicit in
terms of actual endpoint subset volumes. All integer tilts and every
continuous direction are included. The two large fibers are assumed to
be simplices of equal volume; this is a material restriction.

## Theorem and normalization

Let A,B,C be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in R^d, d>=2, with
B and C simplices, |B|=|C|=V, |A|=a>0, and (A+C)/2 contained in B.
Set S=({-1}xA) union ({0}xB) union ({1}xC). There is a constant rho_d>0,
defined below and depending only on d, such that a/V<=rho_d implies
the existence of y in int(B) satisfying

    H_d(S intersect H) >= (Gamma/2)(2V+a)

for every closed ambient halfspace H containing (0,y), where
Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d. The ambient body conv(S) has exactly these three
integer fibers, so this is an assertion about an actual induced set.
Indeed any endpoint mixture at base zero belongs to (A+C)/2, and any
mixture including B at base zero stays in B.

An affine change in the continuous variables sends B to the standard
simplex conv(v_0,...,v_d), v_0=0, v_i=e_i. It preserves the mixed lattice
and multiplies every fiber volume by the same positive Jacobian. Select
any p_0 in A and apply the shear (z,x) -> (z,x+z p_0). Renaming fibers,
0 belongs to A and C is contained in 2B. Fixing c_0 in C also gives
A contained in 2B-c_0, hence in 2(B-B). These transformations preserve
all halfspaces and all relative masses. In this frame every point of
A union B union C has norm at most R=2 sqrt(d), and V=1/d!.

Write N=d+1, b=1/N, j=ceil(N/2), and let lambda_0,...,lambda_d be the
barycentric coordinate functions of B. Put n_i=grad(lambda_i),
theta_i=n_i/|n_i|, g=(1/N,...,1/N), and

    delta = N^(-N/[2(floor(N/2)+1)])-1/N > 0.

The positivity follows because the exponent's absolute value is less
than one. The normals satisfy 1<=|n_i|<=sqrt(d).

## A determinant margin and fixed endpoint credits

For any p in A, the simplex L_p=(p+C)/2 lies in B and has volume 2^-d V.
Its barycentric vertex matrix P is nonnegative and column stochastic,
with |det(P)|=2^-d. Sort its row maxima p_1>=...>=p_N. Replace the first
row by the sum of all rows, then subtract p_i/2 times this ones row
from row i>=2. Hadamard's inequality gives

    2^(-(N-1)) <= |det(P)|
                  <= N^(N/2) 2^(-(N-1)) product_(i=2)^N p_i.

Since j>=2, the product is at most p_j^(N-j+1). Thus p_j>=b+delta.
Let h_i=max_C lambda_i and define fixed compact subsets

    A_i={p in A: lambda_i(p)+h_i >= 2b+delta},
    c_i=|A_i|,  cbar=(sum_i c_i)/N.

The row maxima of P are (lambda_i(p)+h_i)/2. At each p, at least j
coordinates are >=b+delta. Consequently every p belongs to at least j
of the sets A_i, and

    0<=c_i<=a,             cbar >= (j/N)a.                 (1)

The indices need not be the same for different p. This is an integrated
indicator count, not a common-direction assumption. Also the inclusion
L_p in B proves width_C(lambda_i)<=2.

We need the following credit estimate uniform over nearby normals.
Let r=a/V, and suppose a point y in B obeys

    max_i(lambda_i(y)-b)_+ <= delta/8,
    r^(1/d)<=delta/8.

For every unit u with |u-theta_i|<=delta/(24R sqrt(d)) and every real
beta, the endpoint cap contributions to

    u.x+beta z >= u.y

sum to at least c_i. Here is a proof including the tilt optimization.
Multiplying by |n_i| and adding the constant in lambda_i reduces the
continuous functional to f=lambda_i+v.x, |v|<=delta/(24R). If h=max_C f,
W=width_C(f), a homothetic copy of C at an f-maximizer shows that the
cap f>=h-W r^(1/d) has volume at least a. For any tilt, either the
C-cap has mass at least a, or its threshold is greater than that value.
In the latter case the A-threshold is less than
2f(y)-h+W r^(1/d). Therefore the endpoint sum is at least

    |A intersect {f >= 2f(y)-h+W r^(1/d)}|.                (2)

For p in A_i put kappa=R|v|<=delta/24. Boundedness, the definition of
A_i, and width_C(lambda_i)<=2 imply

    f(p)+h >= 2b+delta-2kappa,
    f(y) <= b+delta/8+kappa,       W<=2+2kappa.

As r^(1/d)<=1, subtracting the right side of the threshold in (2)
leaves at least delta-2(delta/8)-2(delta/8)-6kappa >=delta/4>0.
Thus (2) contains A_i and proves the claimed credit. No small diameter
of A and no restriction on beta has been used.

## A simplex cap estimate and a single chosen point

If a halfspace through y in int(B) has precisely vertex i strictly on
its positive side and all other vertices on its nonpositive side, its
intersection with B is a simplex with edge ratios t_k in (0,1], k!=i.
If alpha_i>0 and alpha_k<=0 are its affine values at vertices, then
t_k=alpha_i/(alpha_i-alpha_k). The identity sum lambda_k(y)alpha_k=0
gives sum_(k!=i) lambda_k(y)/t_k=1. AM-GM yields

    |B intersect H|=V product_(k!=i)t_k
                   >= V d^d product_(k!=i)lambda_k(y).    (3)

This includes vertices on the cutting hyperplane. Select the point by

    lambda_i(y)=b+(c_i-cbar)/(N Gamma V).                  (4)

These values sum to one. If r<Gamma, they are positive and determine a
single point in int(B). Moreover

    |lambda_i(y)-b|<=r/(N Gamma),
    |y-g|<=sqrt(d) r/(N Gamma).                            (5)

Fix

    eta=min{delta/(24R sqrt(d)), 1/(8N sqrt(d))}.

If r<=Gamma/(4d), then for |u-theta_i|<=eta every other vertex k!=i
has u.(v_k-y)<0. Indeed theta_i.(v_k-g)=-1/(N|n_i|), whereas the
perturbation from replacing theta_i,g by u,y is bounded by

    eta |v_k-y| + |y-g|
        <= sqrt(2)/(8N sqrt(d)) + 1/(4N sqrt(d))
        < 1/(2N sqrt(d)).

We used that the diameter of B is sqrt(2). As y is in the interior and
the weighted sum of all vertex values is zero, vertex i is then
strictly positive. Thus (3) applies uniformly throughout each of these
oriented neighborhoods.

Let E_d=2^d-d-1>0 and set s_k=N(lambda_k(y)-b). Then
|s_k|<=r/Gamma, sum s_k=0. When r/Gamma<=1, the elementary product
expansion gives

    product_(k!=i)(1+s_k)
      >= 1-s_i-E_d(r/Gamma)^2.

There are binom(d,l) degree-l terms, each bounded in absolute value by
(r/Gamma)^l<=(r/Gamma)^2 for l>=2. Combining (3), this expansion and
the fixed endpoint credit gives, for every tilt and every direction
within eta of theta_i,

    H_d(S intersect H)
      >= Gamma V - (c_i-cbar) - (E_d/Gamma)(a^2/V) + c_i
      >= Gamma V + (j/N)a - (E_d/Gamma)(a^2/V).             (6)

Put k_d=j/N-Gamma/2>0. If r<=Gamma k_d/(2E_d), (6) is at least
Gamma V+Gamma a/2+k_d a/2, strictly above the required mass.

## Every remaining direction

For the fixed standard simplex define

    F(u)=|B intersect {u.(x-g)>=0}|/V, |u|=1.

Classical continuous Grunbaum gives F(u)>=Gamma. Its usual single-cap
equality characterization says that equality requires a pyramid with
base parallel to the cut and the cap on the apex side. For a simplex,
these equality directions are exactly theta_0,...,theta_d: each apex
is a vertex, and its other d vertices determine the opposite facet.
This uses only the classical continuous theorem and its equality case.

The function F is continuous by dominated convergence, because each
boundary hyperplane has d-volume zero. Thus

    G_d=min_{|u|=1, min_i|u-theta_i|>=eta}(F(u)-Gamma)>0.   (7)

The minimum is attained on a compact set disjoint from the equality
directions. This set is nonempty: u=-e_1 has distance sqrt(2) from
each positive coordinate normal except theta_1, from which it has
distance 2, and distance sqrt(2-2/sqrt(d)) from theta_0, all >eta.
In (7), F is an explicitly defined integral over one fixed simplex;
there is no unknown extremizer or mixed-depth assumption in G_d.

Let omega_(d-1) denote the (d-1)-volume of the Euclidean unit ball and
L_d=d! omega_(d-1). Every hyperplane section of B has area at most
omega_(d-1), since B lies in the unit ball. Fubini along a unit normal
therefore shows that moving its threshold by h changes normalized cap
mass by at most L_d |h|. By (5), for a direction in (7), the middle
fiber alone contributes at least

    V[Gamma+G_d-L_d sqrt(d) r/(N Gamma)].                 (8)

Writing Q_d=L_d sqrt(d)/(N Gamma)+Gamma/2, the condition
r<=G_d/(2Q_d) makes (8) greater than Gamma V+Gamma a/2.

## Explicit positive range and boundary cases within this theorem

Define

    rho_d=min{(delta/8)^d, N Gamma delta/8, Gamma/(4d),
               Gamma k_d/(2E_d), G_d/(2Q_d)} >0.           (9)

All constants are finite, positive and depend only on d. For 0<r<=rho_d,
(4) is an interior point and satisfies the uniform credit hypotheses.
Every nonzero continuous normal belongs either to one of the closed
eta-neighborhoods, handled by (6), or to the compact complement, handled
by (8), after normalization. Both arguments allow every real integer
tilt. The cap boundary is null in each full-dimensional fiber.

A purely integer normal through (0,y) gives the closed halfspace z>=0
or z<=0. Its mass is respectively 2V or V+a. Both dominate
Gamma(V+a/2), since r<=Gamma/(4d)<1 and 0<Gamma<1/2. These caps carry
the full middle-fiber boundary mass, which has been included. Any
halfspace containing (0,y) contains its parallel closed halfspace
through that point, so the asserted inequality holds for all containing
halfspaces, not just through-point cuts.

The theorem deliberately requires d>=2 and a>0 with full-dimensional
fibers. It makes no assertion here about d=0, d=1, null endpoint mass,
more integer bases, unequal large volumes, or nonsimplex large fibers.
Those omissions restrict this auxiliary theorem, not the scope of the
active OC goal. In particular this proof is not a full resolution.

## Dependency record

The determinant and uniform-credit arguments above reproduce the needed
parts of `candidate 986ab1688d049a3b`
and `candidate 6b774d09877ca348`, both already
independently audited. All remaining inequalities and compactness steps
are proved above. The sole non-elementary external input is classical
continuous Grunbaum with its standard equality case, as precisely
recorded in `candidate e2c55c91458e1e8c`.
